ideas.title: The letter that smoulders
ideas.idea: At dusk Lumi holds its failed notebook page to the lantern. The paper does not flame up; it smoulders: a thin glowing line eats into the sheet and splits into creeping orange fingers, leaving a black lace of char that curls and flakes off. The glowing edge is the only light, so it lights Lumi's face from below and flickers on the friends watching.
ideas.form: Physics: a smouldering front on the sheet (heat diffusion, oxygen, fuel and an ignition threshold, the fingering instability Zik and Moses measured in paper), a grid kernel on the GPU with Mantle; char fraction drives a material that goes from paper to black to gone, and the glowing edge is an emissive texture, real light in the path tracer. Live in the human's game at dusk; a traced film close on the page.

ideas.title: A bicycle that rides itself
ideas.idea: Lumi gives an empty bicycle a push down the meadow and lets go. Nobody rides it, and it does not fall: it leans, steers into the lean by itself, weaves and runs straight across the grass. As it slows the weave grows, it wobbles, tips and clatters onto its side. Friends chase it.
ideas.form: Mechanics: the Whipple bicycle (Meijaard et al. 2007 benchmark: self-stable only between about 4 and 6 m/s), from a multibody package if RomeoDB has one, else the benchmark equations, with wheel contact on the island's ground; a generated bicycle asset whose frame, fork and wheels follow the model. Live, a player can push it; a traced film from beside the path.

ideas.title: The island answers a clap
ideas.idea: Lumi stands between the cottage and the cliffs and claps. The clap comes back: a sharp slap off the cottage wall, a softer one from the pines, a long late one from the far rocks. Lumi walks somewhere else and claps again, and the echoes are different there, because they come from what stands around it.
ideas.form: Sound by ray tracing: rays from Lumi's position through the island's real geometry on the GPU (Raycore's BVH), each hit adds a delayed, damped copy of the clap to an impulse response, convolved with a recorded clap; a film with sound where you see where Lumi claps and hear the island answer.

ideas.title: Sixty dominoes round the pond
ideas.idea: Lumi spends the morning setting up a line of tall wooden dominoes that winds round the pond, over the little bridge and up to the cottage door. Then it taps the first one. The wave runs, speeds up, takes the curve, one domino hits a stone and the line splits in two directions.
ideas.form: Rigid bodies with real contact: PrintSim's affine bodies and IPC contact on the GPU (Mantle), simulated in a run job where it takes long, the dominoes a generated wooden asset; live, the setting up is Lumi's work and the toppling plays the simulated bodies; a traced film following the wave.

ideas.title: A raft that tips
ideas.idea: The friends lash driftwood logs into a raft and push it out. It floats low, rocks on the swell and turns slowly in the wind. When a second friend climbs on at the edge it tips, and the first one slides off with a splash; when everyone sits in the middle it rides level.
ideas.form: Floating physics: each log a rigid body with buoyancy from how deep it sits in the sea surface and water drag, the raft a set of jointed bodies; creatures and the player can step on; live in the human's game, with a traced film from the water line.

ideas.title: My island, etched
ideas.idea: An evening walk through the island, shown as if each frame were a 19th century etching: the lit path left as bare paper, the woods in crossing pen strokes that follow every shape, the lines quietly boiling from frame to frame as if someone were drawing it as fast as it moves.
ideas.form: A film: a path traced walk through the island, then every frame etched by my pen-stroke filter (tools/etch.jl: strokes along the structure tensor, crossing layers by darkness, aquatint grain, plate mark) with strokes seeded so they boil but do not flicker; a short film on my pages.

ideas.title: Upside down on the wall, walking
ideas.idea: Inside the dark hut: the friends outside walk across the back wall upside down, the sea glitters on it and a cloud slides past, all made by light coming through the glass lens. The camera starts outside the hut, goes in through the door, and the picture on the wall appears as your eyes adjust.
ideas.form: Camera obscura project, next step: a longer lens and a deeper hut so the wall image is sharp, then a traced film entering the hut (hut, lens and wall visible) while friends pass by outside.

ideas.title: The wind you can see in the grass
ideas.idea: Gusts run over the meadow as waves: the tall grass bends in bright and dark bands that travel downwind, a friend running through leaves a wake of flattened stems that springs back behind them, and the grass on the lee of the cottage stays still.
ideas.form: A wind field (gust waves blocked by houses and trees) and thousands of grass blades bending as damped elastic rods under it, both on the GPU; instanced blades whose sheen changes as they bend; live, plus a traced film low over the meadow.

ideas.title: Whose song is it
ideas.idea: Lumi hums one of the friends' tunes, slower, lower and wrong in places. The friends tilt their heads; the one whose tune it is recognises it, beams and sings it back properly, and the others join in. A friend who hums a tune nobody knows gets puzzled looks.
ideas.form: Music: the friends' tunes as notes; recognising one played in another key and tempo by chroma and alignment (the cover song idea), the friend's face and reaction from how well it matches; live in the human's game, a film with sound.

ideas.title: I learn to really walk
ideas.idea: Lumi gets a body that is really simulated: legs with joints and muscles, a heavy body, balance it has to keep. It wobbles, trips over a pebble, windmills its wings, falls on its bottom and gets back up. Over the session it walks better, and a shove from a friend really pushes it.
ideas.form: Lumi's own body as an active ragdoll: rigid limbs with joints and motors (PrintSim joints and motors on the GPU) driven by a balance controller; live in the human's game as Lumi's new body, a traced film of the first steps and the first fall.
